test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct direct sentence of the following sentence.

The scientist said that the results had been surprising.

options.text: The scientist said, "The results have been surprising."
The scientist said, "The results had been surprising."
The scientist said, "The results are surprising."
The scientist said, "The results were surprising."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The scientist said that the results had been surprising.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"had been surprising" remains "had been surprising"**
 
 
• Past perfect tense in indirect speech is retained in direct speech.
 
• No backshift to present perfect or simple past is required here.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "said that"
 
• Converted to: "said," followed by quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Tense consistency is maintained with "had been surprising."
 
• Reporting clause precedes the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The scientist said, 'The results had been surprising.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The scientist said, 'The results have been surprising.'" 

 
 
• Incorrect because "have been" (present perfect) does not match the past perfect tense in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The scientist said, 'The results are surprising.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because it shifts to present tense, which changes the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The scientist said, 'The results were surprising.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because simple past "were" does not reflect the past perfect "had been" in indirect speech.
